subject: Capacity map & deal-led pool requests — US/EU/APAC next 12 months

Date: 2026-05-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot -> prod capacity ask (US/EU/APAC)

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — AtlasAI is excited to move from pilot to production. We ran a quick forecast with our product team and need help sizing dedicated capacity tied to our roadmap. High level:

- Phase 1 (P0, next 3 months): 8 sustained H100-equivalent GPUs in US (low-latency region) for inference with ~10k daily requests.
- Phase 2 (Q3–Q4): additional 10 H100-eq in EU for GDPR workloads and 4 in APAC for experiments.

We need SLA targets (p95 < 250ms for 2k token median), a sense of burst capacity, and the ability to pin model versions. Attached is a quick Excel with our projected token volumes (atlas_capacity_matrix.xlsx).

Key asks: a) recommended pool sizing per region, b) how reserved vs burst pricing would apply, c) timeline for getting Dedicated pools up.

Joe

Diego / Aditya — looping in from the EU partner side. For GDPR-compliant Dedicated pools we typically colocate in our FRA and AMS sites. Latency to AtlasAI's EU customers looks good from those sites, and we can offer private network interconnects.

A couple of notes:
- H100 instances give better perf for long-context models; A100s are more cost-effective for short prompts.
- If you need a soft burst buffer, we can stage a small mixed A100 pool to absorb 2–3x spikes while the H100 reserved capacity is prioritized.

Happy to run network tests — tell me the IP ranges and we’ll schedule.

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, Joe Snow <joe.snow@atlas.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-15T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity map & deal-led pool requests — initial sizing proposal

Diego / Joe / team — attaching a proposed pool diagram and a concise sizing summary (see attached proposed_pool_diagram.png). Below is the textual summary to avoid waiting on attachments: 

Summary (recommended reserved + burst):
- US (primary, low-latency): 12 H100-equivalent reserved, + 6 A100 burst nodes for peak smoothing. Rationale: Atlas's median token length + streaming needs favor H100 for sustained lower latency.
- EU (GDPR): 8 H100-equivalent reserved, + 4 A100 burst. Data residency: all EU traffic pinned to EU pool.
- APAC (exploratory): 3 A100 reserved initially (cost-effective), scale to 6 if Q4 commitments met; provide optional cross-region fallback to US with explicit consent.

Operational notes: 
- Autoscaling windows: set conservative cpu/gpu thresholds for Q1 post-provisioning, then iteratively loosen with telemetry.
- Caching: enable prefix cache + model KV sharing in the US pool — expected 20–30% token cost reduction for Atlas's prompt patterns.
- Provisioning timeline: 4–6 weeks for baseline pools in US/EU if we have a signed MO/AD and commit to a 6-month reserved minimum for the reserved portion. Burst capacity can be added within 48–72 hours.

Pricing guidance (ballpark):
- Reserved H100-eq (monthly committed): priced per GPU-hour with stepped discount at 6/12 months.
- Burst A100 nodes billed at on-demand premium.

Next actions:
1) Confirm reserved minimums per region (we propose US:12, EU:8, APAC:3).
2) Diego to circulate an addendum to the SOW / MO (Lauren will approve discount band).
3) Grace to align invoicing cadence.

Attaching diagram now.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.app

Joe — thanks for the quick turnaround and good alignment with Aditya. Per our conversation and the sizing proposal above, AtlasAI confirmed the following committed pools:

- US: 12 H100-equivalent reserved + 6 A100 burst
- EU: 8 H100-equivalent reserved + 4 A100 burst (data pinned in EU)
- APAC: 3 A100 reserved initially (convert to H100 if Q4 commit hit)

Decisions / next steps:
- Lauren to approve a 10% commit discount for a 6-month reserved minimum (Lauren, please confirm by Tue 5/20).
- Diego will circulate an MO addendum linking these pool counts to DEAL ATL-7843 and include the provisioning SLAs (4–6 week baseline).
- Grace will draft invoice cadence and attach the finance terms.
- Atlas to sign the MO; we’ll stage burst nodes immediately after signature, reserved capacity after the commit window closes.

We have attached the signed non-binding LOI / MOU for internal routing (signed_mou.pdf). Once Lauren confirms pricing band, I’ll open the procurement doc in HubSpot and route to finance — link below.
